INTERNAL REVENUE SERVICE
Department of the Treasury

NOTICE OF DEFICIENCY (Letter 3219)
Tax Year: 2022
Notice Date: April 7, 2025

Taxpayers: Michael A. Okafor and Diane R. Okafor
Joint Return, Filed: April 15, 2023
Address: 4417 Larkspur Ridge Rd, Cary, NC 27519

This letter is a NOTICE OF DEFICIENCY as required by law. The Internal Revenue Service has
determined a deficiency in your income tax for the year(s) shown above. If you want to contest
this deficiency in court before making any payment, you have 90 days from the date of this letter
(150 days if addressed to a person outside the United States) to file a petition with the United
States Tax Court, pursuant to Internal Revenue Code (IRC) Section 6213(a).

Summary of Adjustments

1. Unreported income (bank deposits method) ..................... $47,600
2. Disallowed Schedule C vehicle expense (substantiation) ........ $9,800
3. Disallowed Schedule C home office expense (substantiation) .... $4,200
4. Disallowed Schedule C contract labor expense (no Forms 1099) .. $4,400

Total adjustments to taxable income ............................. $66,000
Recomputed deficiency in tax .................................... $17,850
Accuracy-related penalty, IRC Section 6662(a) (20%) ............. $3,570
Total amount you owe ............................................ $21,420

Explanation of Adjustments

Item 1: Our examination of your business bank account (Piedmont Trust Bank, acct ending 4471)
identified total deposits of $186,400 during 2022. Your return reported gross receipts of
$138,800 from Okafor Strategic Consulting. Because you did not provide records reconciling the
$47,600 difference during the examination, it is treated as unreported gross receipts under IRC
Section 61(a).

Items 2-4: Deductions claimed on Schedule C were disallowed in full because contemporaneous
records adequate to substantiate business purpose, amount, and time were not provided at the time
of examination, as required under IRC Section 162(a) and the recordkeeping requirements of IRC
Section 6001.

Penalty: The accuracy-related penalty under IRC Section 6662(a) is asserted based on a
substantial understatement of income tax.

If you do not file a petition with the Tax Court within the time period described above, the
deficiency will be assessed and you will receive a bill.

/s/ R. Falkenberg
Technical Services, Area 4
